task: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Spirit Airlines

merged.claim: Spirit Aviation Holdings (formerly NYSE: SAVE) is private; ownership passed to former creditors on emerging from first Chapter 11 on 2025-03-12 via exchange of ~$795M funded debt for equity plus a $296.1M equity rights offering (7,770,054 shares); no PE sponsor or founder owner.

Spirit Airlines, LLC is a wholly owned operating subsidiary of Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc.; the March 2025 reorganization made the holding company the parent and converted Spirit Airlines, Inc. into an LLC, with new parent shares and warrants issued to certain creditors.

As of 2026-04-15, largest disclosed 5% holders of Spirit Aviation Holdings were PIMCO (9.5%), Arena Capital Advisors (9.1%), AllianceBernstein (8.4%), Cyrus Capital (7.6%), Ares Management (7.0%), M&G (6.5%) and Citadel (5.7%).
Spirit Airlines, Inc. changed its name to Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. on 2025-03-13.
After the 2026-05-02 wind-down, Spirit's remaining assets are controlled by the bankruptcy estate and court-supervised process, and common-stock holders were told to expect a complete loss.
Spirit Airlines total operating revenues were $958.5M in Q3 2025 (three months ended 2025-09-30, Successor).
Spirit Airlines total operating expenses were $1,093.4M in Q3 2025, exceeding revenue by about $135M.
Spirit Airlines had $646.6M of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash as of 2025-09-30.
Spirit Airlines had $408M unrestricted cash as of 2025-06-30, with its $275M revolver fully drawn (per Moody's via Reuters).
Spirit Airlines had about $2.4B of long-term debt (most due 2030) at its second Chapter 11 filing in August 2025.
Spirit Airlines had negative free cash flow of about $1B as of end of Q2 2025.
Spirit Airlines combined FY2025 net loss was about $2.7B (predecessor plus successor, including $2.1B reorganization items).
Spirit combined FY2025 total revenue was about $3.7B.
Spirit Aviation Holdings reported FY2025 operating revenue of $3,796,747,000 (combined predecessor and successor periods).
Spirit Aviation Holdings reported a successor-period operating loss of $481,511,000 for 2025-03-13 to 2025-12-31.
Spirit Aviation Holdings reported a predecessor-period operating loss of $287,199,000 for 2025-01-01 to 2025-03-12.
Spirit had $864.3M of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash as of 2025-12-31.
Spirit Aviation Holdings had unrestricted cash and cash equivalents of $272,959,000 as of 2025-12-31.
Spirit January 2026 revenue was $250.3M, with operating loss of $42.0M (operating margin -17%); net loss was $125.1M, including $83.1M of other/reorganization expenses.
Spirit had adjusted cash and restricted cash of $822M at end of January 2026, versus $867M at end-December 2025.
Spirit Aviation Holdings reported long-term debt before current maturities and unamortized discounts of $1,258.7M as of 2025-12-31.
Spirit Aviation Holdings had $1,609.4M of debt classified within liabilities subject to compromise as of 2025-12-31.
Spirit Aviation Holdings reported $124.4M of accounts payable within liabilities subject to compromise as of 2025-12-31 (pre-petition, subject to automatic stay).
From the 2025-08-29 petition date Spirit ceased making principal and interest payments and ceased accruing interest on long-term debt reclassified to liabilities subject to compromise.
Spirit's 2025 Form 10-K reported a 17.4% reduction in the pilot and flight-attendant workforce from headcount rationalization and restructuring.

Spirit Airlines, LLC reported ending cash/restricted cash of $266,849,907 as of 2026-07-31 in its unaudited monthly operating report (pooled debtor accounts, excludes intercompany flows, not freely available liquidity).

Spirit Airlines, LLC held cash of $231,834,781 as of 2026-08-31 per its August monthly operating report (filed 2026-09-22, docket 1632), as transcribed by a secondary source; not verified unrestricted liquidity.
Spirit Airlines, LLC's July 2026 monthly operating report showed 76 full-time employees as of 2026-08-01, versus 9,229 as of 2025-09-30.
Spirit had $3.6B total outstanding debt at its November 2024 Chapter 11 petition, with 21,000 employees/contractors and a 213-aircraft A320 fleet (51 owned).
Spirit filed its first Chapter 11 on 2024-11-18 in SDNY with $3.6B total debt, after the JetBlue merger was blocked and with $2.5B+ cumulative losses since 2020.
Spirit launched a $350M equity rights offering ($14.00/share) on 2024-12-30; it closed at emergence with $296,107,812 consideration (7,770,054 shares and 13,380,504 warrants).

Spirit emerged from first Chapter 11 on 2025-03-12, equitizing about $795M of funded debt, with $350M equity investment, $840M exit secured notes due 2030 and a $275M exit revolver; repaid the $300M 2024 DIP and $300M revolver.
The $275M exit revolver matures in 2026 and was reduced to $250M on 2026-09-30.
Spirit's revolver matures March 2028 (per Moody's).

On 2025-08-15 Spirit transferred an additional $50M cash to a pledged account with its credit-card processor (USB) and agreed to holdbacks of up to $3M/day until fully collateralized, in exchange for extending the processing agreement to 2027-12-31.
On 2025-08-21 Spirit fully drew its $275M exit revolver to fund operations and credit-card collateral requirements, and warned it might not survive a year without significantly more cash.
Spirit disclosed 'substantial doubt' about going-concern ability with Q2 2025 results, repeated in its Q3 2025 Form 10-Q.
Spirit Aviation Holdings' 2025 Form 10-K (dated 2026-03-16) stated substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern within one year and warned liquidation could be required.

Spirit Aviation Holdings and five affiliates filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in SDNY on 2025-08-29 (lead case 25-11897; Spirit Airlines, LLC case 25-11896, jointly administered), its second Chapter 11 in less than a year.
Spirit Airlines, LLC is the borrower under the interim DIP order dated 2025-08-29, with Spirit Aviation Holdings and affiliates as guarantors.
On 2025-10-14 Spirit Airlines, LLC entered a DIP credit agreement providing up to $475M of aggregate new-money term loans, with certain subsidiaries as guarantors.

On 2025-10-31 the Bankruptcy Court approved a multi-draw senior secured super-priority DIP facility of up to $1.2B, including up to $475M new-money loans and up to $750M roll-up of pre-petition secured notes.
Spirit drew a $200M new-money DIP loan on 2025-10-14.
Spirit drew a $50M new-money DIP loan on 2025-11-07.

On 2025-12-15 Spirit amended the DIP credit agreement and drew a $100M third new-money round; $50M (net of OID) was immediately usable and $50M stayed encumbered pending progress toward standalone reorganization, strategic transaction or exit financing.
Aircraft lessor AerCap terminated Spirit aircraft leases ahead of the second Chapter 11; Spirit later sought court approval to reject remaining aircraft leases.
An Examiner was appointed in Spirit's Chapter 11 case (SDNY) in October 2025.
Spirit's post-bankruptcy plan projected a 2026 net loss of $111M and a 2027 net profit of $55M on $2.6B revenue; overtaken by the May 2026 shutdown.

On 2026-03-13 Spirit filed a plan of reorganization, disclosure statement and RSA with consenting DIP lenders; it later pivoted to wind-down, seeking to auction LaGuardia slots, campus, loyalty program and equipment, and to sell/abandon 28 owned aircraft and 18 spare engines.
By 2026-04-15 Spirit was reported at risk of imminent liquidation amid a jet-fuel price surge; by April 18 it sought a federal bailout and the administration considered a controlling stake.

Spirit ceased all flights on 2026-05-02 and began an orderly wind-down/liquidation after being unable to obtain additional funding, stating it needed hundreds of millions of dollars of liquidity it could not procure; it attributed the failure to materially higher oil/fuel prices and other pressures, and the proposed March bondholder restructuring did not preserve an operating airline.
Spirit's bailout talks (~$500M proposal with the Trump administration) collapsed before the 2026-05-02 shutdown.

Spirit CFO Fred Comer said there was no viable path to continued operations; Reuters reported on 2026-05-04 that Spirit planned to retain about 150 employees in wind-down and cut to about 40 after three months.
On 2026-05-05 Judge Sean H. Lane approved Spirit's wind-down procedures and granted aircraft lease rejection and sale motions; the U.S. Trustee's suggestion to convert to Chapter 7 was not pressed.
CNBC reported on 2026-05-04 that about 17,000 direct and indirect Spirit workers lost jobs; CEO Dave Davis remained with about 130 other employees to oversee closure.
Employee health insurance ended on 2026-05-02; Florida WARN notices showed more than 4,850 layoffs (2,529 FLL, 551 Dania Beach, 181 MIA, 796 MCO plus 796 MCO inflight/ops center).

NBC reported on 2026-05-14 a proposed employee class action in Spirit's bankruptcy court alleging layoffs without required WARN notice and seeking unpaid wages and benefits; some former employees reported missing final paychecks (unadjudicated allegations).

On 2026-05-02 Spirit said flights bought directly by credit/debit card would be automatically refunded to the original payment method, while vouchers, credits and Free Spirit points would be addressed later through bankruptcy; customer service was no longer available.
Spirit told Reuters on 2026-05-03 that most customers who paid by card had been refunded by the evening of May 2, with a small percentage still processing.

Broward County (FLL operator) asserted liens on Spirit aircraft for postpetition administrative claims on 2026-05-05; trade counterparties, airports, lessors and insurers forced modifications to the wind-down order.
Claims bar dates: general proofs of claim due 2026-01-27, governmental units 2026-02-25, pre-wind-down administrative expense claims 2026-07-27.
As of 2026-10-14 Spirit's liquidation was ongoing, with a simulator sale, continued aircraft-sale disputes, and the proposed data sale hearing adjourned to 2026-11-06.

S&P downgraded Spirit to 'CCC' from 'CCC+' on 2024-06-05, outlook negative, citing 2025 maturities ($1.1B loyalty bonds due Sep 2025, $500M convertibles 2026), less than adequate liquidity and likely distressed exchange.
Fitch downgraded Spirit to 'CCC-' from 'CCC+' on 2025-08-18, citing operational losses, deteriorating liquidity and default risk.
Fitch downgraded Spirit's loyalty-program debt to 'CCC-' from 'B-' on 2025-08-18, with recovery rating RR4 from RR3.

Moody's downgraded Spirit's corporate family rating two notches to Caa3 from Caa1 on 2025-08-22 (PDR Caa3-PD, SGL-4 from SGL-3, outlook negative), citing higher than expected cash burn and forecasting over $500M cash burn in 2025.
Spirit's Moody's rating fell from B2 (2023) to Caa3 (2025); S&P projected a $600M free cash flow deficit for 2025, with negative outlooks.
S&P downgraded Spirit Airlines LLC to D from CCC on 2025-09-02 after the 2025 Chapter 11 filing.
Fitch downgraded Spirit Airlines' Long-Term IDR to D from CCC- on 2025-09-04 after the second Chapter 11 filing, and downgraded senior secured debt to C/RR4.
On 2026-05-06 Fitch affirmed Spirit Airlines, LLC's IDR at D and withdrew it the same day following the decision to cease operations and liquidate.
On 2026-05-21 S&P withdrew all ratings on Spirit Airlines LLC, including EETC ratings, because of insufficient information.
CEO Ted Christie exited on 2025-04-07 weeks after emergence and CCO Matt Klein stepped down; an office of the president ran the company until Dave Davis was named CEO.

Spirit discontinued service in 11 U.S. cities from October 2025, furloughed ~270 pilots from Nov 1, downgraded 140 captains, and confirmed 1,800 flight-attendant furloughs (nearly one-third of cabin crew) by Dec 1, 2025.
Spirit cut about 150 corporate/market jobs and exited several markets on 2025-11-05.
Spirit's fleet shrank from 214 aircraft pre-bankruptcy toward a planned 76 by mid-August 2026, with international routes slashed.

c1.note: The FY2025 10-K confirms emergence on 2025-03-12 and the 7,770,054 shares for about $296.1M. Davis Polk confirms the $795M debt equitization. The unit's own URL (c0c27bf1) was not a valid link, so it was not opened. I did not separately confirm that no PE sponsor or founder owns the company.

c2.note: The 10-K says Former Spirit converted to a Delaware LLC, was renamed Spirit Airlines, LLC, and became a wholly owned subsidiary of Spirit Aviation Holdings. I did not check the warrant issuance to creditors.

c3.note: The 10-K/A holder table as of 2026-04-15 matches every holder and percentage. The PIMCO figure includes warrant shares.

c4.note: The filings confirm the Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. name and the 2025-03-12 emergence as that entity. I found no primary source giving 2025-03-13 as the name-change date. The unit may also conflate the holding-company reorganization with a rename.

c5.note: Press confirms Spirit ceased operations on 2026-05-02 and is being liquidated under court supervision. The cited 10-K/A, signed 2026-04-30, predates the wind-down and does not contain it. I found no evidence it says common-stock holders should expect a complete loss, so the attribution to that source fails.

c6.note: The Q3 2025 10-Q shows total operating revenues of $958,524K for the three months ended 2025-09-30 (Successor).

c7.note: The 10-Q shows operating expenses of $1,093,439K, which is an operating loss of about $135M.

c8.note: Cash and cash equivalents of $250.5M plus restricted cash of $396.1M total $646.6M. Unrestricted cash is only $250.5M.

c9.note: Reuters reports Moody's citing $408M of unrestricted cash at the end of Q2 and a fully drawn $275M revolver. I did not open the Yahoo page. The figures come from search-result text of the Reuters article.

c10.note: Financier Worldwide reports $2.4bn of long-term debt, most due 2030, at the Aug 29, 2025 filing. This is a search-snippet confirmation, and the 10-Q's debt lines at 9/30 are consistent, though they total roughly $2.7B.

c11.note: The Q2 2025 10-Q shows H1 operating cash flow of about -$473M and capex of about -$21M, so free cash flow was about -$0.5B. That is not about -$1B. Q2 liquidity fell only about $200M.
